newsitem.title: USA: CU Bancorp, Bancorp Hawaii merge.
newsitem.headline: CU Bancorp, Bancorp Hawaii merge.

text.p: CU Bancorp said it has definitively agreed to merge with Bancorp Hawaii Inc, the parent of Bank of Hawaii, for $15.34 per CU Bancorp common share.
The price is payable in a combination of Bancorp Hawaii common stock and cash, with the stock portion to remain between 60 to 80 percent, the company said.
CU Bancorp shares closed Monday up 1/8 at 13-1/4. Bancorp Hawaii shares closed up 5/8 at 45.
The deal would be completed no later than the third quarter of 1997 if it is approved by CU Bancorp shareholder and regulators.
CU Bancorp will operate as a subsidiary of the Hawaiian holding company. Stephen Carpenter will remain CU Bancorp president and David Rainer will remain chief executive, the company said.

"Bancorp Hawaii has indicated that it is pursuing a strategy of geographical diversification spanning the Asia-Pacific region and aimed at capturing trade flows across the Pacific," Rainer said. "This acquisition will be their first acquisition in California, which is an important part of that strategy."
Bancorp Hawaii is the largest Hawaii-based financial organisation. Its principal subsidiary, Bank of Hawaii, is the state's largest commercial bank.
CU Bancorp is the holding company of California United Bank.
